move: lines drop in one by one, squash on impact, spring back, exit
how: An aurora photo at 35% opacity zooms out slightly (scale 1.1 to 1.02, linear over 5s) behind a left-aligned stack of four headline lines in clipped rows, the third in mint, with a small numbered index on the right. Each line falls from yPercent -110 / opacity 0 with power3.in over 0.55s, starting at 3% and every 0.42s after; on landing it squashes to scaleY .86 (power2.out, 0.09s, origin at the baseline) and recovers to 1 with elastic.out(1,.4) over 0.5s. The index fades in from x 20 at 24%. From 85% the lines drop out through the bottom (yPercent 110, power3.in, 0.07s stagger) in the same order and the index fades, ending on the photo.
adapt: Change the line strings and count, which line is highlighted, the accent colour, the index labels and the background image. Keep the power3.in fall plus the squash-and-elastic recovery and the 0.42s cadence.
port: mount(el, shot) builds .bg, the .stack of .row/.ln pairs from shot.lines and the .num index; animate(el, shot, D) loops the lines and returns a gsap.timeline with each fall at (0.15+i*0.42)/5*D, the squash 0.5s later, the exit at 0.85D. Scope gsap.utils.toArray to el.
caveats: from() on .num needs immediateRender:false if built lazily
